overview: Based on the published agenda, the Village of Kronenwetter's Community Life, Infrastructure and Public Property Committee was scheduled to address infrastructure and development matters on August 3, 2026, including a potential data center moratorium, oak wilt ordinance, trail planning, and the 2027-2036 capital improvements budget.
committee: Community Life, Infrastructure and Public Property (CLIPP) Committee

agenda.item: Approval of July 6, 2026 CLIPP Committee Meeting Minutes
4-Way Stop on County Road XX and Terrebonne Drive
Resolution 2026-011 Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on New Data Center Development Applications and Referring the Matter to the Planning and Utility Committees for Further Study
2027-2036 Capital Improvements Program (CIP) Budget – 1st Draft as of 07/31/2026

discussions.item: 4-Way Stop on County Road XX and Terrebonne Drive
discussions.body: The committee was scheduled to discuss old business regarding a four-way stop intersection on County Road XX and Terrebonne Drive. This item was set for discussion and possible action.
The committee was scheduled to consider an Oak Wilt Ordinance as new business. This item was set for discussion and possible action regarding the regulation of oak wilt management in the village.

discussions.item: Resolution 2026-011 Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on New Data Center Development Applications
discussions.body: The committee was scheduled to consider Resolution 2026-011, which would establish a temporary moratorium on new data center development applications and refer the matter to the Planning and Utility Committees for further study. This item was set for discussion and possible action.

The committee was scheduled to discuss potential future trails in Kronenwetter as new business. This item was set for discussion and possible action regarding trail planning and development in the community.

The committee was scheduled to review the first draft of the 2027-2036 Capital Improvements Program Budget as of July 31, 2026. This item was set for discussion and possible action on the village's long-term capital infrastructure planning.

publicComment: Public comment was indicated on the agenda with a 15-minute time limit and three-minute period per person.
